content: Sickle cell disease is the most prevalent single-gene disorder and the most common hemoglobinopathy, with a high prevalence in various populations worldwide. Managing dental complications in individuals with sickle cell disease requires specific considerations due to three primary factors. First, the blood disorder directly impacts dental and oral tissues, leading to several orofacial abnormalities. Second, the chronic nature of the disease and its severe systemic consequences may cause individuals to neglect their oral health. Third, the treatment of dental complications must be tailored to the systemic condition and unique needs of these patients to avoid worsening their overall health. Currently, there are no clear or comprehensive guidelines for managing dental complications in this population, and in many areas, such guidelines are entirely absent. This review was conducted to analyze existing evidence in the literature and provide a foundation for clinical care in treating dental complications in individuals with sickle cell disease. It serves as an update to a previously published review. The objective of this review was to evaluate methods for treating dental complications in people with sickle cell disease. To achieve this, a thorough search was conducted. The Cochrane Cystic Fibrosis and Genetic Disorders Review Group's Haemoglobinopathies Trials Register was utilized, which includes data from electronic database searches and manual searches of journals and conference abstracts. The last search of this register was performed on August 1, 2019. Additionally, nine online databases were searched, including PubMed, Google Scholar, ClinicalTrials.gov, the WHO International Clinical Trials Registry Platform, the Literature in the Health Sciences in Latin America and the Caribbean database, African Index Medicus, Index Medicus for the South-East Asia Region, Index Medicus for the Eastern Mediterranean Region, and the Indexing of Indian Medical Journals. Reference lists of relevant articles and reviews were also examined, and experts in hematology, dentistry, and related fields, as well as organizations, pharmaceutical companies, and researchers, were contacted. The last search of these sources was conducted on November 7, 2019. The selection criteria focused on identifying published or unpublished randomized controlled trials (RCTs) that evaluated treatments for dental complications in individuals with sickle cell disease. Two review authors planned to independently extract data and assess the risk of bias in the included studies using standard Cochrane methodologies. However, no studies meeting the inclusion criteria were identified. The main result of this review is that no randomized controlled trials were found that assessed interventions for treating dental complications in people with sickle cell disease. Consequently, the authors concluded that there is a significant need for well-designed randomized controlled studies in this area. Such research is essential to determine the most effective and safe methods for managing dental complications in this patient population.
